purpose: Stress-test the book author's sound+meaning uniqueness method by asking whether the same permissive matching procedure produces plausible competitors in the independently documented Yeniseian lexicon. A competitor is NOT an etymology; it only measures how underconstrained the author's inference is.
method_rule: Do not infer Yeniseian origin merely because a control resembles the Chinese/book form.
A control weakens only the claim that a Hebrew sound+meaning resemblance is uniquely diagnostic.
Chronology, historical Chinese sound, donor-language historical sound, geography/contact, systematic correspondences and morphology remain separate gates.
Modern northern dialect forms cannot be projected back to fourth-century Jie without an attestation chain.
The book author's claimed Hebrew/Aramaic match is recorded as SOURCE CLAIM until independently verified.

rows.book_context: ethnonym; author compares 羯胡 with Jehu/Jehud
rows.author_meaning: Jehu / Jew/Judah-related ethnonym in the author's model
rows.source_date_gate: 羯 is securely historical in late Han-Jin sources; exact 4C transcription value requires historical reconstruction
rows.yeniseian_control: Arin kit/qit; Imbak ke:t/ket; Pumpokol kit; Ket/Yugh ke:t
rows.reason: Werner independently documents a family-wide kVt 'person' set. This does not prove 羯 is Yeniseian, but it gives a historically relevant alternative to modern jie~Jehu resemblance, especially because historical 羯 retained a final stop.
rows.next_gate: 4C Chinese sound lattice + historical Jehu/Jehud sound + ethnonym semantics + migration/contact

rows.book_context: kin term; author treats ab as a Hebrew survival
rows.source_date_gate: book ranges across old texts and modern northern usage; exact historical Chinese attestations must be separated
rows.yeniseian_control: Pumpokol ab; Arin bvap/ipä/ajap; Assan/Kott/Imbak op~ob
rows.reason: Werner independently records Pumpokol ab = father. Under the author's own sound+meaning criterion, Hebrew is therefore not a unique match. This does not establish borrowing or common origin because parental terms are especially vulnerable to nursery-language and areal convergence.
rows.next_gate: earliest Chinese/Inner Asian attestations + nursery-word null model + contact chronology

rows.book_context: modern/northern first-person pronoun treated by author as preserved Jie speech
rows.source_date_gate: modern dialect evidence; continuity back to 4C Jie is currently unproven
rows.yeniseian_control: Arin aj/ä; Assan aj/ja; Imbak äde/ad/di; Kott aj/ai/ja; Pumpokol ad; Ket/Yugh at
rows.reason: Werner does not supply a close an/ami first-person equivalent. The author's strongest problem here is not a competing Yeniseian word but the millennium-plus attestation gap between modern dialect 俺 and a claimed 4C Jie source.
rows.next_gate: historical Chinese dialect chronology of 俺 + Biblical Hebrew historical form + areal pronoun survey

rows.book_context: author interprets 阿彌 before a personal name as 'my people/my son'
rows.author_meaning: my people / my son in author's interpretation
rows.source_date_gate: must first establish exact Jin-period phrase, syntax and whether 阿彌 is a name/title/kin form
rows.yeniseian_control: Arin first-person possessive b-/be-/me-; Werner reconstructs Arin possessive *abe from pronoun aj
rows.reason: Yeniseian supplies an independent first-person possessive system but not a close Ammi lexical match. It is a control against overinterpreting possessive semantics, not an alternative etymology.
rows.next_gate: retrieve original 阿彌 sentence + name syntax + Hebrew ammi morphology + Chinese transcription chronology

rows.book_context: 石勒表文 '流離屯厄'; author rejects ordinary Chinese reading and glosses it as hometown/village
rows.source_date_gate: Jin-history sentence is historical; whether 屯厄 is a foreign lexical unit must be demonstrated syntactically
rows.yeniseian_control: Arin xalgontura / turd; Assan turd / tura-ken; Kott turd
rows.reason: Werner independently records turd/tura-type 'village' forms in multiple southern Yeniseian branches. Under a permissive Duwr~屯厄 comparison this is an obvious competing match. It still does not show that 石勒's 屯厄 is Yeniseian.
rows.next_gate: Chinese syntax/lexical history of 屯厄 + 4C sound + Hebrew dor/duwr history + Turkic/Iranian controls

rows.book_context: modern/regional girl term linked by author to Yaldah
rows.source_date_gate: modern/regional forms and medieval Chinese 丫頭 history must be separated from 4C Jie
rows.yeniseian_control: Assan alit-jali; Kott alitali < alit jali; Arin big'al'a / kemebatalpalti; Pumpokol pikola
rows.reason: Several Yeniseian girl terms contain alit/jali-like material. This is exactly the kind of result a loose phonetic search can generate in an unrelated candidate pool, showing why systematic sound rules are necessary.
rows.next_gate: history of 丫頭 and 東北鴨蛋兒 + Hebrew yaldah historical pronunciation + chance-match baseline

rows.book_context: food name interpreted by author as Shemesh and solar symbolism
rows.source_date_gate: food-name chronology and earliest forms must be established independently; symbolic solar interpretation is later inference
rows.yeniseian_control: Pumpokol hichem/hixem; Arin ega/Eja; Assan/Kott ega-type
rows.reason: Pumpokol hixem/hichem = sun is independently documented and is phonetically suggestive under exactly the loose sound+meaning method used by the book. It is a control, not evidence that 燒賣 is Yeniseian.
rows.next_gate: earliest 梢麥/燒賣 attestations + historical Chinese reading + Hebrew Shemesh + food-history null

rows.book_context: Later Zhao ceremonial fan/object name interpreted as manna and then as ancestral bread memory
rows.source_date_gate: 莫難 is directly an object/fan name in the transmitted Later Zhao material; food semantics are the author's inference
rows.yeniseian_control: Arin bread itpek/itprak/itpak; Pumpokol koita/kojta/talan; Ket/Yugh na:n~n'e:n
rows.reason: Werner gives no strong Yeniseian manna-like equivalent; Ket/Yugh na:n is only a partial resemblance. The author's larger problem is the jump from a 4C ceremonial object name to food/manna memory.
rows.next_gate: original 莫難扇 textual tradition + 4C sound + object-name etymology + Hebrew man/manna morphology

rows.book_context: author links brother terms and 鮮卑 阿干 to Hebrew ach
rows.source_date_gate: 鮮卑 阿干 and Chinese 阿哥 histories must be independently dated; cannot be treated as Jie evidence by association
rows.yeniseian_control: Arin bamagal/amagel; Pumpokol xej-kit/akil/alik/bic; Ket/Yugh bisep-type
rows.reason: Werner does not offer a clean ach-like brother word. The methodological issue is instead population mixing: a Xianbei term cannot automatically be used to prove Jie Hebrew ancestry.
rows.next_gate: earliest 阿干 sources + Xianbei/Mongolic/Turkic comparanda + Hebrew ach historical sound

rows.book_form: 上帝／昊天上帝 religious layer
rows.book_context: book interprets Jie religion as survival of Israelite/Jewish monotheism
rows.author_match: YHWH / Biblical monotheism rather than a direct phonetic word match
rows.source_date_gate: Later Zhao religious practice must be separated from modern family oral tradition and from the author's Biblical interpretation
rows.yeniseian_control: Arin es; Assan ös/es; Imbak es/is/ejs; Kott es; Pumpokol ec; Ket/Yugh es
rows.reason: Werner documents a widespread native Yeniseian God lexeme es. This does not identify Later Zhao religion, but it supplies an independent northern religious vocabulary that must be considered before treating monotheistic-looking material as uniquely Hebrew.
rows.next_gate: primary Later Zhao ritual vocabulary + 佛圖澄 context + comparative Yeniseian religion + Iranian/Buddhist/local cult alternatives

summary_rules.EXACT_SOUND_MEANING_CONTROL: A competitor with essentially the same loose phonetic shape and meaning under the author's own method; destroys uniqueness but does not prove alternative etymology.
summary_rules.STRONG_CONTROL_UNDER_AUTHOR_LOOSE_PHONET: A very suggestive competitor only if the author's permissive phonetic tolerance is allowed; demonstrates false-positive risk.
summary_rules.NO_STRONG_YENISEIAN_PHONETIC_CONTROL: Werner does not supply a close competitor; the author claim still must pass chronology and historical-sound gates.
summary_rules.RELIGIOUS_LEXICON_CONTROL_NOT_ETYMOLOGY: Controls interpretive uniqueness at the cultural/religious level rather than word ancestry.
